question: What does park() cost with the free-spot index compared with the stage 1 scan, and has it been measured?
answer_hinglish:
Short answer: stage 1 mein park() har spot ko scan karta tha, yaani O(spots). Stage 2 se ek FreeSpotIndex hai -- har size ki ek min-heap -- aur README ka claim hai park() ab O(sizes x log spots) hai. Aur important baat: yeh NOT benchmarked hai. README aur PLAN dono saaf likhte hain 'Not benchmarked' / 'the claim is the complexity, not a benchmark'. Interview mein main koi number nahi bolunga, sirf complexity.

Kyun sizes x log spots? Vehicle jitne sizes mein fit hota hai (motorcycle 3, car 2, truck 1), utni baar index se poocha jaata hai 'is size ka nearest free spot'. Har nearest() ek heap peek hai, aur stale entries hon toh pop -- pop O(log n). Sizes sirf 3 hain, toh practically yeh log spots hai.

Ek detail jo log miss karte hain: reserve() mein do jagah nearest() call hota hai -- pehle LOT_FULL pre-check (fittingSizes(vehicle).some(...)), phir strategy ka choose(). Dono milake bhi constant x log n hi hai, aur doosri baar heap top already saaf hota hai, toh woh sirf peek hai.

Correctness ka proof benchmark nahi, oracle test hai: invariants.test.ts har park ko stage 1 wale full scan (expectedSpot) se compare karta hai, dono strategies ke saath.
why_needed: Bada lot ho aur rush hour mein har gate har car par saare spots scan kare toh cost spots ke saath linear badhti hai. Index se per-park kaam lagbhag constant rehta hai.
real_world_analogy: Purana tareeka: guard poori building mein ghoom ke khaali spot dhoondhta hai. Naya: har size ki ek 'next khaali spot' wali list guard ke haath mein hai, sabse upar wala hi dekhna hai.
how_it_works: Spots nearest-first order mein numbered hain (level, phir position). Har size ki heap mein un spot numbers ki entries hain; heap top = sabse chhota number = nearest. nearest(size) top dekhta hai; agar woh spot ab free nahi hai toh pop karke agla dekhta hai.
in_this_project: src/free-index.ts ka comment: 'nearest() is O(log n) amortised, release is O(log n), reserve is O(1)'. ParkingLot.reserve() pehle LOT_FULL check index se karta hai, phir this.allocation.choose(vehicle, this.index). README 'Free-spot index' section: 'park() is O(sizes x log spots) instead of a scan of every spot ... Not benchmarked.'
advantages: Per-park cost spots ke saath sirf log se badhta hai
Strategy ka code chhota: sirf size order decide karta hai
Correctness har park par full scan se check hoti hai (oracle test)
disadvantages: Koi measured number nahi -- chhote lot par scan bhi utna hi fast ho sakta hai
Extra memory: heaps, inHeap array, numberOf map
common_mistakes: Complexity ko benchmark result bata dena
Bhool jaana ki reserve() mein nearest() do baar chalta hai
Amortised aur worst-case ko mix karna

question: Lazy deletion leaves stale entries in the heap. Why is the heap still bounded, and what is the amortised cost of nearest()?
answer_hinglish:
Bounded isliye hai kyunki har spot ki heap mein AT MOST EK entry ho sakti hai, aur yeh inHeap flag guarantee karta hai. Toh total entries <= spots, chahe kitna bhi churn ho. Test isko seedha check karta hai: index.entryCount() kabhi spots.length se zyada nahi (3000 random steps ke har step par).

Mechanism: spot lene par heap ko touch hi nahi karte (reserve O(1)) -- entry stale ho jaati hai lekin inHeap[i] true rehta hai. Spot free hone par released() pehle inHeap dekhta hai; agar purani entry abhi bhi heap mein hai toh push NAHI karta -- woh purani entry phir se valid ho gayi, kyunki nearest() spot.isFree live check karta hai. Push sirf tab hota hai jab entry pehle pop ho chuki thi (inHeap false).

Amortised cost: har push ki hui entry zindagi mein max ek baar pop hoti hai. Toh total pops <= total pushes, aur pushes = initial free spots + released() calls jo sach mein push karte hain. Matlab ek nearest() call kabhi kai stale entries pop kar sakta hai (worst case k x log n), lekin poore run par per-operation average O(log n) hai.

Bina inHeap ke har release ek naya push hota, aur ek spot jo baar baar le-chhoda jaata hai uske kai duplicate entries jamaa ho jaate -- heap churn ke saath badhta. Mutation S10 ne yahi kiya aur 2 tests fail hue.
why_needed: Lazy deletion bina bound ke ek slow memory leak ban jaata hai: busy lot mein din bhar ke releases heap ko spots se kai guna bada kar dete.
real_world_analogy: Notice board par 'khaali spot' ki parchiyan. Spot bhar jaaye toh parchi turant nahi hatate; jab koi padhta hai aur spot bhara milta hai tab phaadte hain. Aur ek spot ki ek hi parchi lagti hai -- purani lagi ho toh nayi nahi.
how_it_works: nearest(): loop { top = peek; agar spots[top].isFree return; warna pop aur inHeap[top]=false }. released(spot): i = numberOf.get(spot); agar inHeap[i] toh return; warna push(size, i) aur inHeap[i]=true.
in_this_project: src/free-index.ts: private readonly inHeap: boolean[]; nearest() pop ke baad this.inHeap[i] = false; released() mein 'if (i === undefined || this.inHeap[i]) return;'. entryCount() comment: 'Never more than the number of spots (tested)'. Test free-index.test.ts 'a spot released while its old heap entry is still there is not added twice' expect(index.entryCount()).toBe(2).
advantages: Memory O(spots), churn se independent
reserve O(1): heap ko chhoona hi nahi padta
Ek spot ka re-release free hai agar entry abhi heap mein hai
disadvantages: Ek nearest() call ka worst case kai pops ho sakta hai (latency spike)
Ek extra boolean array aur spot -> number map rakhna padta hai
common_mistakes: Amortised O(log n) ko har call ka worst case samajhna
inHeap ko pop par false karna bhool jaana -- tab spot kabhi wapas push nahi hoga
Release par hamesha push karna

Worst case mein ek nearest() kitni entries pop kar sakta hai?
Indexed heap (decrease-key / remove) se compare karo

question: Why does the lot keep availability counters per (level, size) row instead of counting free spots when a board asks?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki board ko jo chahiye -- 'level 0 par compact kitne free' -- woh har change par ek counter +1/-1 karke O(1) mein maintain ho jaata hai, aur availability() phir sirf rows copy karta hai: O(rows), O(spots) nahi. Rows = levels x (us level par jo sizes hain), jo spots se bahut kam hain.

Constructor mein har level ke liye har size ka total gina jaata hai aur sirf wahi row banti hai jiska total > 0 hai (rows Map, key 'level:size', insertion order = board order). Phir count sirf teen jagah badalta hai: reserve (-1), cancel (+1), exit (+1) -- dono +1 forget() ke through. confirm aur beginExit count nahi badalte, isliye event bhi nahi bhejte. Ek hi function changeFree(spot, delta) counter badalta hai aur usi waqt event emit karta hai, toh counter aur event kabhi alag nahi ho sakte.

Risk yeh hai ki counter drift kar jaaye -- kahin decrement bhool gaye. Isliye invariants test har step ke baad check karta hai ki availability() ke free ka sum == snapshot mein free spots ki ginti, aur DisplayBoard ki rows == availability(). Stage 1 ka mutation 'availability ignores the level' 11 tests se pakda gaya.

Trade-off: ek chhota sa duplicated state (counter) vs har read par scan. Reads (boards) writes se zyada hote hain, toh counter sahi choice hai -- bas use test se guard karna padta hai.
why_needed: Display boards baar baar padhte hain. Har read par saare spots scan karna bada lot hone par bekaar kaam hai, jabki change waise bhi lot ke andar ek hi jagah hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Har floor ke entrance par ek counter wala gatekeeper: car andar to -1, bahar to +1. Board dekhne ke liye floor ghoomna nahi padta.
how_it_works: rows: Map<'level:size', {level, size, free, total}>. changeFree(spot, delta): row = rows.get(rowKey(spot.level, spot.size)); row.free += delta; events.emit(freeze copy). availability() = rows ki copies.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts: 'private readonly rows = new Map<string, Row>(); // insertion order = board order', rowKey, changeFree, availability() comment 'O(rows)'. invariants.test.ts checkInvariants: freeOnBoard === free spots in snapshot.
advantages: availability() O(rows)
Counter aur event ek hi function mein: drift ka ek hi source
Board order deterministic (Map insertion order)
disadvantages: Duplicated state: spot states aur counter alag alag sach bol sakte hain agar koi path changeFree skip kare
Naya count-changing operation add karo toh changeFree call yaad rakhna padta hai
common_mistakes: confirm par bhi count ghata dena (double count)
Counter test na karna, sirf spot states test karna
Har size ki row bana dena chahe level par woh size ho hi nahi

Counter drift detect kaise karoge production mein?

question: What happens to this design at 10x and 100x the spots and levels? Where would it hurt first?
answer_hinglish:
Honest answer: kuch measure nahi kiya gaya, toh main complexity se reason karunga, numbers se nahi.

Jo achhe se scale karta hai: park() -- FreeSpotIndex ki heaps se O(sizes x log spots); 100x spots par log sirf thoda badhta hai. Counter update O(1). DisplayBoard event apply karna O(1) (Map.set). Memory sab O(spots): spots array, spotsById, inHeap, numberOf, heaps (entries <= spots, tested).

Jo linear hai aur pehle chubhega:
1. availability() O(rows) -- bahut saare levels par har call saari rows copy karta hai. DisplayBoard ise sirf constructor mein ek baar padhta hai, toh theek hai, lekin koi baar baar availability() poll kare toh cost badhegi.
2. activeTickets getter O(entries) -- har call saari entries filter karta hai; tests aur invariants isko loop mein use karte hain, production path mein nahi.
3. snapshot() O(spots) -- sirf tests/debugging ke liye.
4. Events: har count change par har listener synchronously chalta hai. Listeners badhe toh park() ki latency listeners ke saath linear.

Asli wall complexity nahi, architecture hai: sab ek Node process mein, memory mein, koi persistence nahi. 100x lot ka matlab aksar kai entrances, kai processes -- aur README kehta hai multi-process ke liye claim database mein chahiye (conditional UPDATE / unique constraint), jo built nahi hai. 'Nearest' bhi sirf lowest level, then position hai, ek entrance ke saath.
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki tum complexity claim ke limits jaante ho aur bata sakte ho kaunsa hissa pehle tootega.
real_world_analogy: Ek chhoti dukaan ka register system mall mein le jao: billing fast rahega, lekin ek hi cashier counter (single process) bottleneck ban jaayega.
how_it_works: Per-operation cost: reserve = O(sizes x log n) amortised + O(listeners). exit = release O(log n) + O(listeners). availability = O(rows). activeTickets = O(entries). snapshot = O(spots).
in_this_project: src/free-index.ts complexity comment; src/parking-lot.ts availability() 'O(rows)', get activeTickets filter, snapshot() 'for tests and debugging'. README 'NOT implemented': 'Persistence and more than one process', 'Distances: nearest means lowest level, then lowest position; one entrance.'
advantages: Hot path (park/exit) log ya constant hai
Memory linear aur bounded
disadvantages: Single process, in-memory: horizontal scale ka koi raasta nahi abhi
Synchronous listeners lot ki latency mein jud jaate hain
Koi benchmark nahi, toh constants unknown
common_mistakes: Big-O ko throughput number bana dena
Index ko hi scale ka poora jawab samajhna jabki process model asli limit hai
Test-only O(n) getters ko production hot path samajhna
follow_up_questions: Kai entrances ke saath 'nearest' kaise badlega?
Do processes ek lot share karein toh claim kahan jaayega?
Benchmark harness kaisa likhoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: In-memory single process ne code simple aur synchronous claims safe rakhe (JavaScript ek synchronous block beech mein nahi todta). Wahi choice scale-out ko rokti hai: state kisi aur process ke saath share nahi ho sakti.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Process crash = saari state gayi (koi persistence nahi). Ek slow listener har park() ko slow karega. Reservation jiska gate process mar gaya kabhi saaf nahi hota (README: koi expiry sweep nahi).
advanced.alternatives: Spot state database mein rakho aur nearest free spot index-backed query se nikalo; counters ko same transaction mein update karo; events outbox se bhejo. Ya per-lot ek process (sharding by lot) aur har lot ki state uske owner process mein.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x: in-memory design theek lagta hai (complexity ke hisaab se), measure karke confirm karna hoga. 100x ya kai entrances: process model, persistence aur distance model badalna padega -- yeh sab README mein not implemented hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Benchmark harness (spots, churn, sizes ke saath), listener cost ka metric, activeTickets ko hot path se door rakhna, aur persistence + multi-process claim database mein.

question: Event delivery is synchronous inside the lot's method. What does that cost, and what would a slow listener do to park()?
answer_hinglish:
Cost seedha hai: reserve(), cancel() ya exit() tab tak return nahi karta jab tak har listener ne event handle nahi kar liya. EventQueue.emit() lot ke method ke andar se call hota hai (changeFree se), aur emit queue drain karke hi wapas aata hai. Toh park() ki latency = lot ka kaam + sab listeners ka kaam. Ek listener jo 50 ms ka synchronous kaam kare, har park ko utna slow karega -- aur kyunki Node single-threaded hai, us time mein koi aur gate bhi kuch nahi kar payega.

Async listener (jo promise start karke return kar de) lot ko block nahi karta -- emit sirf synchronous call wait karta hai. Lekin us case mein listener ki error onListenerError tak nahi pahunchegi (promise rejection alag hai), yeh dhyan rakhna padega.

Is project mein yeh theek kyun hai: listeners DisplayBoard jaise hain jo sirf Map.set karta hai, O(1). Kaam bhi ek event per changed row -- ek park par ek event.

Chhoti detail: queue ek JS array hai aur shift() technically O(queue length) hai. Normal case mein queue mein ek hi event hota hai; sirf re-entrant listeners queue badhate hain, toh yeh practically issue nahi.

Production mein boards network ke paar honge. Tab main listener ko sirf event ko ek buffer mein daalne dunga (cheap, synchronous), aur ek alag async sender use bhejega -- taaki lot ka hot path network par wait na kare. Yeh built nahi hai.
why_needed: Observer ka hidden cost: subject ka har operation observers jitna slow ho jaata hai. LLD round mein yeh follow-up common hai.
real_world_analogy: Gatekeeper har car ke baad saare floor managers ko phone karta hai aur sabka 'theek hai' sun ke hi agli car andar leta hai. Ek manager lamba baat kare toh line ruk jaati hai.
how_it_works: changeFree -> events.emit(event) -> queue.push -> agar delivering nahi toh loop: shift, har listener ko synchronously call (try/catch). Loop khatam -> delivering=false -> lot method aage badhta / return karta.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts changeFree reserve() aur forget() ke aakhir mein call hota hai ('last: listeners see the finished change'). src/events.ts emit() ka for-loop listener(next) seedha call karta hai. DisplayBoard ka listener sirf this.rowsByKey.set(key(row), row).
advantages: Simple: event ke baad lot aur listeners consistent hain
Ordering guaranteed, koi scheduler nahi
Errors ek jagah (onListenerError)
disadvantages: Har listener ka cost lot ki latency mein
Single thread: ek slow listener saare gates ko rokta hai
Async listener ki rejection onListenerError tak nahi aati
common_mistakes: Listener mein network call await karna aur sochna lot ko farak nahi padega
Queue ko async delivery samajhna -- yeh sirf ordering ke liye hai, delivery ab bhi synchronous hai
follow_up_questions: Async listener ki error kaise pakdoge?
Buffer full ho jaaye toh kya karoge?
Listener ka cost kaise measure karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Synchronous delivery ordering aur consistency deta hai (listener event ke waqt lot ko consistent dekhta hai) lekin coupling bhi: subject ki latency observers par depend karti hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Listener infinite loop ya bahut bhaari kaam kare toh poora process ruk jaata hai -- try/catch sirf throw bachata hai, slowness nahi. Ek re-entrant listener jo har event par lot change kare, queue ko kabhi khaali nahi hone dega.
advanced.alternatives: queueMicrotask/setImmediate se async delivery (lot fast, lekin listener ko lot ab event se aage dikhega); ek outbox buffer + background sender; ya pub/sub broker agar boards alag processes mein hain.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada boards = zyada listeners = har park ka cost linear badhta hai. Us waqt ek hi fan-out listener (buffer) rakho aur boards ko bahar se feed karo.
advanced.production_improvements: Per-listener time ka metric, slow listener par warning, network boards ke liye buffer + batch sender, buffer ka max size aur drop/resync policy.

question: The lot has one entrance and 'nearest' means lowest level then position. How would you support several entrances with their own nearest spot, and what does it cost?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle clear karun: yeh implement nahi hai. README 'NOT implemented' mein likha hai 'Distances: nearest means lowest level, then lowest position; one entrance', aur PLAN 'Not in scope' mein 'multiple entrances with nearest to THIS entrance distances'.

Mera design: FreeSpotIndex already generic hai -- constructor spots ka ek array leta hai aur us array ka index hi priority hai ('spot numbers (index in the lot's nearest-first list)'). Heap sirf numbers compare karti hai. Toh har entrance ke liye spots ko us entrance se distance ke order mein sort karke ek alag FreeSpotIndex bana sakte hain. Lazy deletion phir bhi kaam karega, kyunki free/not-free ka sach ParkingSpot.isFree hai, jo sab indexes share karte hain.

Lot mein badlaav: index ek nahi, Map<entrance, FreeSpotIndex>. reserve() ko entrance chahiye (gate apni entrance batayega), aur LOT_FULL check aur strategy dono us entrance ka index use karenge. forget() mein index.released(spot) ab HAR index par call hoga.

Cost: memory E x spots (E entrances), release O(E x log n), park ab bhi O(sizes x log n). Reserve O(1) hi rehta hai kyunki heap touch nahi hoti. Entrances kam hote hain (2-6 typical), toh yeh theek hai.

Testing: invariants test ka oracle bhi entrance-aware banana padega -- full scan jo distance se sort karke pehla free fitting spot de -- aur har park ko us se compare karna.
why_needed: Asli lots mein kai gates hote hain; gate A se aane wali car ko gate B ke paas wala spot dena bekaar hai. Yeh classic LLD extension question hai.
real_world_analogy: Mall ke har gate par alag 'nearest khaali spot' wali list -- spot ek hi hai, par har gate ki list apne hisaab se sorted hai.
how_it_works: E indexes, har ek spots ki apni permutation par. Spot lena: kuch nahi (lazy). Spot chhodna: har index ka released(). nearest(size) us entrance ki heap se.
in_this_project: src/free-index.ts: constructor(private readonly spots: readonly ParkingSpot[]) aur comment 'One heap per size, holding spot numbers (index in the lot's nearest-first list)'. src/parking-lot.ts mein abhi ek hi 'private readonly index: FreeSpotIndex' aur forget() mein this.index.released(spot). allocation.ts ka nearer() level/position compare karta hai -- multi-entrance mein yeh bhi distance-aware banana padega.
advantages: Existing FreeSpotIndex bina badle reuse
Spot state ek hi jagah (ParkingSpot), indexes sirf ordering
Park cost same
disadvantages: Memory aur release cost entrances ke saath linear
nearestFirst ka nearer() ab level/position par nahi chalega; strategy ko distance chahiye
API change: reserve() ko entrance batana hoga
common_mistakes: Ek index mein sab entrances ka distance mix karna
released() sirf ek index par call karna -- doosre gate ko woh spot kabhi nahi milega (S9 jaisa bug)
Distance ke ties ka deterministic order na rakhna
follow_up_questions: Distance static na ho (jaise ek ramp band hai) toh?
Do gates ek hi spot chahein toh kya hoga?
Oracle test kaise update karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: E indexes = simple aur reuse; ek index jo distance query-time par compute kare (k-nearest ya spatial structure) memory bachata hai par complex hai. Entrances kam hain toh E indexes better.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Ek index ko released() na mile toh woh spot us entrance ke liye 'gayab' ho jaata hai jab uski stale entry pop ho chuki ho -- LOT_FULL jabki board par spot free dikhe. Do gates ek saath -- abhi bhi synchronous reserve se safe, kyunki claim spot state par hai, index par nahi.
advanced.alternatives: Per-level heaps + level ka entrance se distance; ya spatial index (grid buckets) agar spots ke coordinates hon; ya database mein ORDER BY distance query with an index per entrance.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut saare entrances (dozens) par E x spots memory aur har release ka E x log n cost dikhega; tab per-zone/per-level grouping se entries kam karni hongi.
advanced.production_improvements: Distance table config se, oracle test entrance-aware, aur ek metric ki gate-wise average walk distance taaki strategy tune ho sake.

question: Several Node processes must serve one large lot. How do the free-spot index and the availability counters change?
answer_hinglish:
Yeh project mein built nahi hai -- sab kuch ek process ki memory mein hai. README kehta hai: 'Several processes sharing a database would need the claim in the database (a conditional UPDATE or a unique constraint on the spot) -- the same idea, moved to where the state lives. Not built.' Main wahi idea index aur counters par lagaunga.

Problem: FreeSpotIndex aur rows Map process-local hain. Do processes ke apne-apne heaps ek hi spot ko free maanenge aur dono reserve kar denge. Synchronous claim sirf ek process ke andar safe hai.

Design: spot ka state database mein. 'Nearest free spot of size X' ek query ban jaata hai -- (size, state, level, position) par index ke saath ORDER BY level, position LIMIT 1, aur claim ek conditional UPDATE: 'set state=reserved where id=? and state=free'. Affected rows 0 = kisi aur ne le liya, agla try. Heap ka kaam database index karta hai, lazy deletion ki zaroorat nahi kyunki query live state par hai.

Counters: (level, size) row ka free count usi transaction mein update karo jismein spot claim hua, warna counter aur spot alag sach bolenge -- wahi drift jisse invariants test bachata hai. Hot row (ek popular level ka counter) par contention aa sakti hai; tab counter ko spot states se periodically derive karna ek option hai.

Events: process ke andar EventQueue nahi chalega; transaction ke saath outbox table mein event likho aur ek publisher boards ko bheje. Yeh sab generic production pattern hai, is repo mein kuch nahi hai.
why_needed: Senior round mein interviewer LLD ko 'ab isse distributed karo' tak le jaata hai. Answer yeh hona chahiye ki claim kahan jaata hai, kyunki wahi correctness hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek register ki jagah teen counters par teen cashier: agar sabke paas apni notebook ho toh ek hi seat do logon ko bik jaayegi. Ek shared register chahiye jisme 'agar abhi khaali hai tabhi likho'.
how_it_works: Claim = conditional write (compare-and-set) at the source of truth. Nearest = indexed ordered query. Counter = same-transaction update ya derived view. Events = transactional outbox.
in_this_project: README 'Concurrency (stage 2)': safe inside ONE Node process; 'NOT implemented': 'Persistence and more than one process'. PLAN Decisions: 'This only holds inside one Node process; several processes sharing a database would need the claim in the database'. In-memory pieces: src/free-index.ts FreeSpotIndex, src/parking-lot.ts rows + changeFree, src/events.ts EventQueue.

-- illustrative (NOT in the repo): claim the nearest free compact spot
UPDATE spots SET state = 'reserved', holder = :ticket
WHERE id = (
  SELECT id FROM spots
  WHERE lot_id = :lot AND size = 'compact' AND state = 'free'
  ORDER BY level, position
  LIMIT 1
)
AND state = 'free';   -- 0 rows updated: someone else won, try again
advantages: Claim wahan jahan state hai: processes ke beech safe
Database index heap ka kaam karta hai
Same two-phase shape (reserve/confirm) bacha rehta hai
disadvantages: Har park ek network round trip + transaction
Hot counter rows par contention
Events ke liye outbox/broker chahiye
common_mistakes: Har process mein in-memory heap rakh ke sochna DB ki zaroorat nahi
Counter ko alag transaction mein update karna
Retry loop ke bina conditional UPDATE
follow_up_questions: Conditional UPDATE 0 rows de toh kitni baar retry?
Counter ki hot row ka contention kaise kam karoge?
Gate process crash ho toh reservation ka kya? (README: koi expiry sweep nahi)

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: In-memory: fast, simple, single process. DB-backed: correct across processes, lekin latency aur contention. Beech ka raasta: lot ko shard karo (ek lot = ek owner process) aur us process mein yahi in-memory design.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Gate process reserve ke baad mar jaaye: spot reserved hi reh jaata (aaj bhi yahi limitation hai, koi expiry sweep nahi). DB mein reserved_at column aur sweeper isko theek karega. Publisher down ho toh boards stale -- outbox se replay.
advanced.alternatives: Redis mein per-size sorted set (score = level/position) aur claim ek atomic script mein; ya ek single-writer process per lot jisko baaki processes request bhejein.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x par DB query + index kaafi hai. 100x aur kai lots par lot_id se partition karo; ek lot ka state ek partition mein rahe taaki claim ek jagah atomic ho.
advanced.production_improvements: Reservation expiry sweeper, idempotent gate retries, outbox publisher with sequence numbers, aur counter reconciliation job jo spot states se counts dobara gine.

question: Walk through EventQueue.emit(). What do the queue and the delivering flag do?
answer_hinglish:
emit(event) teen kaam karta hai: event ko queue mein daalta hai, agar koi aur emit pehle se deliver kar raha hai toh wahi return ho jaata hai, warna khud delivery loop chalata hai jab tak queue khaali na ho.

Step by step: (1) this.queue.push(event). (2) if (this.delivering) return -- matlab hum kisi listener ke andar se re-entrant call mein hain; outer emit() is event ko baad mein drain karega. (3) delivering = true, phir loop: queue.shift() se agla event, aur us event ke liye listeners ki COPY par iterate. Har listener se pehle has() check -- agar woh beech mein unsubscribe hua toh skip. listener(next) try/catch mein; error onListenerError ko jaata hai, aur woh handler bhi throw kare toh ek khaali catch use nigal leta hai. (4) finally mein delivering = false.

Iska result: events exactly us order mein deliver hote hain jisme changes hue, aur ek event tab tak agla shuru nahi hota jab tak woh har listener tak na pahunch jaaye. question: Trace FreeSpotIndex through construction, a reserve, a release and a nearest() call. Which data structure holds what?
answer_hinglish:
FreeSpotIndex ke paas teen cheezein hain: heaps (Map<SpotSize, MinHeap>, har size ki ek heap jisme spot NUMBERS hain), inHeap (boolean[], spot number -> kya uski entry abhi kisi heap mein hai), aur numberOf (Map<ParkingSpot, number>). Spot number = lot ke spots array mein index, jo level phir position ke order mein bana hai -- isliye sabse chhota number = nearest.

Construction: har spot ka number numberOf mein; jo spot free hai uska push(size, i), jo inHeap[i] = true karta hai. Heap size pehli baar push par lazily banti hai -- toh jis size ka lot mein koi spot nahi, uski heap hi nahi, aur nearest() turant undefined deta hai.

Reserve: lot spot.reserve() karta hai; index ko koi call NAHI jaata. Entry heap mein reh jaati hai, stale.

nearest(size): top peek; spots[top].isFree? haan to return. Nahi to pop aur inHeap[top] = false, phir agla top. Matlab cleanup padhne waale ke time par hota hai.

Release: lot ka forget() spot.release() ke baad index.released(spot) call karta hai. released() number nikalta hai; agar inHeap[i] true hai -- purani entry abhi pop nahi hui -- toh kuch nahi karta, woh entry phir valid hai. Warna push.

Ek important baat: index kabhi apna 'free' state nahi rakhta. Sach ParkingSpot.isFree hai; heap sirf candidates ka ordered list hai. Isi liye lazy deletion safe hai -- stale entry kabhi galat answer nahi deti, sirf ek extra pop.
why_needed: Heap se arbitrary element hatana O(n) search ya ek position map maangta hai. Lazy deletion se reserve O(1) aur code chhota rehta hai.
real_world_analogy: Har size ki ek priority line jisme log token number se khade hain. Koi chala jaaye toh line se nikalte nahi; counter par bulaane par dekhte hain woh hai ya nahi.
how_it_works: Source of truth: ParkingSpot.state. Index = per-size min-heap of candidate numbers + inHeap bitmap for dedup. Reads clean up; writes (release) dedup-push.
in_this_project: src/free-index.ts: constructor spots.forEach(...) with numberOf.set aur 'if (spot.isFree) this.push(spot.size, i)'; private push() lazily 'new MinHeap()'; nearest(); released(). src/parking-lot.ts forget(): spot.release(...) phir this.index.released(spot). Test 'skips spots taken since (lazy deletion) and offers them again once released'.

Reserve O(1)
Unknown spot (doosre lot ka) par released() kuch nahi karta
disadvantages: Lot ko yaad rakhna padta hai har free hone par released() bulana
numberOf ek extra Map; object identity par key
common_mistakes: Sochna ki reserve par index update hota hai
released() sirf exit path mein call karna aur cancel (gate failure) mein bhool jaana -- is repo mein dono forget() se jaate hain, isliye ek hi jagah call hai

advanced.failure_scenarios: released() miss ho (S9): spot tab tak milta rahega jab tak uski stale entry pop nahi hui; pop ke baad woh hamesha ke liye gayab -- LOT_FULL jabki board free dikhata. Heap order toota (S11): galat (door ka) spot milega.

question: How does the small MinHeap in free-index.ts push and pop, and why does it store numbers instead of spots?
answer_hinglish:
Yeh ek array-based binary min-heap hai: index i ka parent (i - 1) >> 1, children 2i + 1 aur 2i + 2. Invariant: har parent apne children se chhota ya barabar.

push(x): array ke end mein daalo, phir sift-up -- jab tak parent bada hai, swap karke upar jao. pop(): top (a[0]) yaad rakho, last element nikaal ke root par rakho, phir sift-down -- left aur right DONO children dekho, sabse chhota m chuno, agar m === i toh ruk jao warna swap aur neeche. Ek element bacha ho toh a.pop() ke baad array khaali hai aur sift-down skip hota hai.

Dono children kyun? Agar sirf left dekho toh right subtree ka chhota element neeche reh jaata hai aur heap invariant toot jaata hai -- top par galat spot aayega. Yeh mutation S11 tha ('heap sift-down ignores the right child'): stage 2 par 7 tests fail, stage 3 re-run par 8.

Numbers kyun: spot number = lot ke nearest-first list mein index. Toh 'nearest' ka matlab sirf 'sabse chhota number' -- comparison ek number compare hai, koi comparator function ya level/position logic heap mein nahi. Heap generic aur fast rehti hai, aur ordering ka meaning FreeSpotIndex ke constructor mein diye array ke order se aata hai.

Library kyun nahi: code comment kehta hai 'Small and local instead of a dependency' -- project ki zero runtime dependencies wali decision.
why_needed: Free-spot index ka poora O(log n) claim isi heap par tika hai. Heap ka ek off-by-one ya missed child seedha galat spot allocation hai.
real_world_analogy: Tournament bracket: har match mein chhota number jeet ke upar jaata hai; top par hamesha sabse chhota. Naya player neeche se khelta hua upar aata hai.
how_it_works: Sift-up: while i>0 and a[parent] > a[i]: swap. Sift-down: m = smallest of i, l, r (bounds checked); if m == i break; swap(i, m); i = m.
in_this_project: src/free-index.ts class MinHeap (export nahi hai, sirf FreeSpotIndex use karti hai): size getter, peek(), push(), pop(). Random test 'matches a brute-force scan through 3000 random take / release steps' (60 spots) har step par nearest() ko scan se compare karta hai -- heap order ki galti yahin pakdi jaati hai.

Numbers compare: fast aur simple
Ordering ka meaning bahar se (array order) aata hai
disadvantages: Arbitrary remove nahi (isliye lazy deletion)
Khud likhi heap ke bugs khud test karne padte hain
common_mistakes: Sift-down mein sirf ek child dekhna
Parent index (i-1)/2 bina floor ke
pop mein last element ko root par rakhna jab array khaali ho chuka ho

question: How does DisplayBoard stay correct without ever re-reading the lot?
answer_hinglish:
DisplayBoard constructor mein ek baar lot.availability() padhta hai aur har row ko 'level:size' key se ek Map mein rakhta hai. Uske baad woh lot ko kabhi nahi padhta -- sirf subscribe karke har event ko apni Map mein set kar deta hai. Event poori row hai (level, size, free, total), naya absolute count, delta nahi. Toh rowsByKey.set(key(row), row) hi poora update hai.

Correct kyun rehta hai: lot har count change par exactly ek event bhejta hai (reserve, cancel, exit), change complete hone ke baad, aur EventQueue order guarantee karta hai. Snapshot aur subscribe ke beech koi event miss nahi ho sakta kyunki dono ek hi synchronous constructor mein hain -- JavaScript beech mein koi aur code nahi chalata.

Map ki ek chhoti property bhi kaam aati hai: existing key par set() uski insertion position nahi badalta. Toh board ka order availability() jaisa hi rehta hai, aur test seedha board.rows() toEqual lot.availability() likh sakta hai.

rows() copies return karta hai, render() text banata hai ('L0 small   FULL'), aur close() unsubscribe karta hai -- test dikhata hai ki close ke baad exit hone par board purana count hi dikhata hai.

Comment khud kehta hai: event lost ya out-of-order ho toh board drift karega. Isliye randomized tests har step ke baad board ko availability() se compare karte hain.
why_needed: Yahi Observer ka point hai: board ko lot ke internals ka pata nahi, sirf events ka contract. Aur yeh test karta hai ki events poore aur sahi order mein hain.
real_world_analogy: Stadium ka scoreboard operator: match shuru hone par score likh leta hai, phir sirf announcer ki har announcement update karta hai, khud ground par jaake nahi ginta.
how_it_works: Initial snapshot -> subscribe -> har event: map.set(key, row). Events absolute values carry karte hain, toh ek event dobara apply karna bhi harmless hai; order zaroori hai.
in_this_project: src/display-board.ts: rowsByKey Map, constructor mein lot.availability() loop aur lot.subscribe(...), rows(), render(), close(); key = `${r.level}:${r.size}`. Test events.test.ts 'starts from availability() and follows every change; close() stops it'. invariants.test.ts checkInvariants: expect(board.rows()).toEqual(lot.availability()) // the Observer never drifted.

Update O(1)
Absolute counts: duplicate event harmless

Ek process ke bahar yeh snapshot+subscribe atomic nahi rahega

Subscribe pehle aur snapshot baad mein ek async boundary ke saath karna
close() na karna aur purane boards ko leak karna

question: What is the Observer pattern, and what exactly is observed in this parking lot?
answer_hinglish:
Observer pattern mein ek subject hota hai jiska state badalta hai, aur kai observers jo subscribe karte hain aur har change par notify hote hain. Subject ko observers ke baare mein sirf itna pata hota hai ki 'yeh ek function hai jise event dena hai'. Isse subject aur observers decoupled rehte hain: naya board add karna lot ka code nahi badalta.

Is project mein subject ParkingLot hai aur event type AvailabilityChanged hai -- ek (level, size) row ka naya count: { level, size, free, total }. lot.subscribe(listener) ek unsubscribe function return karta hai. Event sirf tab aata hai jab count badle: reserve (-1), cancel (+1) aur exit (+1). confirm aur beginExit count nahi badalte, toh event nahi -- test 'one event per count change, with the new count; confirm and beginExit emit none' free values [1, 0, 1, 2] expect karta hai.

Observer DisplayBoard hai jo availability() se start karta hai aur phir sirf events apply karta hai. Demo mein ek console listener bhi hai jo '[board] L0 compact -> 1/2 free' print karta hai.

Is implementation ki khaas baatein -- jo plain Observer mein nahi hoti: events ek queue se deliver hote hain (re-entrancy safe), throw karne wala listener report hoke skip hota hai (onListenerError), events frozen hain, aur emit hamesha change complete hone ke BAAD hota hai.
why_needed: Display boards, logs, metrics -- sabko lot ke changes chahiye. Bina Observer ke ya toh lot har board ko jaanta, ya boards baar baar lot ko poll karte.
real_world_analogy: YouTube channel subscribe karna: naya video aaya toh sab subscribers ko notification, channel ko har subscriber ka personal kaam nahi pata.
how_it_works: subscribe adds a function to a Set; lot calls events.emit(row) after each count change; EventQueue calls every subscribed function with the frozen row.

question: What is lazy deletion in a priority queue, and why is it a good fit for the free-spot index?
answer_hinglish:
Lazy deletion ka matlab: jab koi element invalid ho jaaye toh use heap se turant mat hatao; use wahin rehne do, aur jab woh top par aaye tab check karo ki valid hai ya nahi -- invalid ho toh pop karke aage badho. Binary heap mein min nikalna O(log n) hai, lekin kisi arbitrary element ko hatana mushkil hai: pehle use dhoondhna padta hai (O(n)) ya ek alag position map maintain karna padta hai har swap par.

Parking lot mein yeh fit kyun hai:
1. Spot lene ka operation (reserve) bahut common hai, aur lazy deletion mein woh heap ko touch hi nahi karta -- O(1).
2. Validity check sasta aur reliable hai: spot.isFree. Sach ParkingSpot ke paas hai, heap sirf candidates rakhti hai.
3. Spot aksar wapas free hota hai. Agar uski purani entry abhi heap mein padi hai (pop nahi hui), toh released() kuch nahi karta -- entry khud valid ho gayi. Isse duplicates nahi bante.

Lazy deletion ka classic risk hai heap ka stale entries se phoolna. Yahan woh inHeap flag se band hai: ek spot ki max ek entry. Doosra risk: ek single read kai stale entries pop kar sakta hai -- lekin har entry ek hi baar pop hoti hai, toh amortised theek hai.

Yeh technique Dijkstra jaise algorithms mein bhi common hai jahan decrease-key ki jagah nayi entry push karke purani ko top par skip karte hain.
why_needed: Bina lazy deletion ke ya toh har reserve par heap se search karke hatana padta, ya ek indexed heap likhni padti -- dono zyada code aur zyada bugs.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant waiting list: koi bina bataye chala gaya toh list se turant nahi kaatte; jab uska naam pukaarte hain aur woh nahi milta, tab kaat ke agla bulaate hain.
how_it_works: Invalidate = kuch mat karo. Read = while top invalid: pop. Re-validate = agar entry abhi present (inHeap) toh kuch mat karo, warna push.
in_this_project: src/free-index.ts comment: 'Lazy deletion: taking a spot does NOT touch the heap. nearest() pops entries whose spot is no longer free until the top is free. A freed spot is pushed back only if it is not still in the heap (inHeap)'. Test 'skips spots taken since (lazy deletion) and offers them again once released'.
advantages: Invalidate O(1)
Code chhota, koi position map nahi
Validity ka sach ek jagah
disadvantages: Read ka worst case kai pops
Bina dedup ke heap unbounded badh sakti hai
common_mistakes: Dedup (inHeap) ke bina lazy deletion
Validity heap ke andar store karna jo source of truth se drift kare
Amortised aur worst case ko confuse karna
follow_up_questions: Indexed heap (decrease-key) kaise kaam karta hai?
Kab lazy deletion galat choice hogi?
Dijkstra mein lazy deletion kahan use hota hai?

question: What is mutation testing, and what did it tell the author about this test suite?
answer_hinglish:
Mutation testing ka idea: code mein jaan bujh ke ek chhota bug daalo (mutation), poora test suite chalao, aur dekho ki koi test fail hua ya nahi. Fail hua = mutation 'caught'. Koi fail nahi = 'survived', matlab tests us behaviour ko actually check nahi karte, chahe coverage 100% ho. Coverage batata hai code chala; mutation batata hai code ka result kisi ne check kiya.

Is project mein yeh manually kiya gaya: README ke mutation table ka har row ek deliberate bug hai, akela apply, full suite run, phir revert (runner scripts repo ke bahar). Stage 1: 18 mein se 18 caught. Stage 2: 25 naye breaks (S1-S25) plus 12 stage 1 re-run -- sab caught. Stage 3: 63 total, 61 pehli baar mein caught; 2 survivors (S24, S26) test gaps the, close kiye gaye aur ab dono caught hain.

Doosri important finding: kuch breaks sirf EK test se pakde gaye. README stage 2 ke liye list deta hai: S3, S5, S6, S7, S14, S19, S20, S22, S24, M15, M16 -- 'deleting that test would hide them'. Aur yeh warning sach nikli: S24 stage 2 par ek test se pakda gaya tha, stage 3 par 0 failures ke saath survive kar gaya. Ek-test wale catch fragile hain.

Har row ke saath 'Failed' count bhi hai -- S8 (index offers reserved spots) 11 ya 12 tests, S14 sirf 1. Number zyada = behaviour kai jagah se guarded.
why_needed: 171 tests pass hona kuch nahi batata agar woh galat cheez check karte hon. Mutation testing tests ko test karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Fire drill: jaan bujh ke ek nakli fire alarm bajao aur dekho kaun sa sensor/guard react karta hai. Koi react na kare toh woh jagah unprotected hai.
how_it_works: For each mutation: apply alone -> run full suite -> record failed count -> revert. Survivor = missing assertion ya missing test case; fix = naya/better test, phir mutation re-run karke confirm.

Survivors seedha batate hain kaunsa test likhna hai
Re-run purane breaks ko naye code par check karta hai
disadvantages: Manual mutations: sirf wahi bugs jo author ne socha
Har mutation ek full suite run -- time lagta hai
Runner scripts repo mein nahi, toh dobara chalana manual

question: A display board ends up showing an old count after a listener parks a car, and another time a listener that unsubscribed still received an event. How would you debug these (mutations S12 and S15)?
answer_hinglish:
Dono EventQueue ke bugs hain, aur dono README ki mutation list mein hain.

S12 -- nested delivery instead of the queue. Symptom: board ek free dikhata hai jabki lot mein us row ka count kam hai. Investigation: board ki row ko lot.availability() se compare karo (invariants test yahi karta hai), phir listeners ka call order log karo. Dikhega: listener A ne event 1 par lot.park() kiya, us park ka event 2 TURANT nested deliver hua -- B ko pehle event 2 mila, phir purana event 1. B event 1 par khatam hua: stale count. Cause: emit() bina queue ke seedha listeners call kar raha tha. Fix: queue + delivering flag -- re-entrant emit sirf enqueue karta hai. Tests: 'an event emitted by a listener is delivered after the current one reached everyone' (a1 b1 a2 b2) aur re-entrant valet test. Dono stage 2 aur stage 3 par: 2 failures.

S15 -- unsubscribed listener still gets the current event. Symptom: kisi ne board.close() kiya ya listener ne beech delivery mein doosre ko unsubscribe kiya, phir bhi woh call hua. Investigation: listener mein log daalo ki unsubscribe ke baad call aaya ya nahi. Cause: copy par iterate karte waqt has() check missing -- copy mein woh listener abhi bhi hai. Fix: 'if (!this.listeners.has(listener)) continue;'. Test 'unsubscribing during delivery stops delivery to that listener at once'. README: stage 2 par 12 tests fail, stage 3 re-run par 1.
why_needed: Observer bugs silent hote hain: koi exception nahi, bas board galat number dikhata hai. Inhe sirf order aur state comparison se pakad sakte ho.
real_world_analogy: S12: do announcements overlap ho gayi aur aakhri sunne wale ko purani wali yaad reh gayi. S15: kisi ne newsletter unsubscribe kiya par is hafte wali phir bhi aa gayi.
how_it_works: S12 fix: queue serializes events globally. S15 fix: copy (so new subscribers wait) + has() (so removed ones stop now).

Randomized test board vs availability() har step par compare karta hai

common_mistakes: Board drift ko lot ka counter bug samajh ke galat jagah dhoondhna

question: Four index bugs were injected: reserved spots offered (S8), freed spot not given back (S9), a spot pushed while still in the heap (S10), and sift-down ignoring the right child (S11). What symptom does each give and what catches it?
answer_hinglish:
Har bug ka symptom alag hai, isliye debug ka raasta bhi alag.

S8 -- index offers reserved spots (11 failures stage 2, 12 stage 3). nearest() 'free' ki jagah kuch aur check kare toh woh reserved spot de dega. Lot khud validate karta hai (!spot.isFree), toh reserve() STRATEGY_BUG phenkega, ya LOT_FULL pre-check galat pass hoga. Symptom: valid park par STRATEGY_BUG. Pakadne wale: 'a reserved spot is not offered to the next car' (LOT_FULL expect) aur oracle comparisons.

S9 -- freed spot not given back (10 / 11). Tricky: spot turant gayab NAHI hota. Agar uski stale entry abhi heap mein hai, nearest() use phir dega. Woh tab gayab hota hai jab ek nearest() ne us entry ko pehle hi pop kar diya tha. Symptom: kabhi kabhi LOT_FULL ya door ka spot, jabki board free dikhata. Investigation: invariants test ka oracle (expectedSpot) har park par mismatch dikhata hai.

S10 -- push while still in heap (2 / 2). Answers sahi rehte hain! Duplicate entries sirf extra pops hain. Symptom: memory badhti hai. Isliye sirf entryCount wale assertions pakadte hain: 'not added twice' test (toBe(2)) aur random test ka entryCount <= spots.length.

S11 -- sift-down ignores right child (7 / 8). Heap order toota, top par minimum nahi. Symptom: nearest spot nahi, koi door ka spot. Pakadne wala: 3000-step brute-force scan comparison aur invariants oracle.

Lesson: S10 jaisa bug correctness tests se nahi, sirf resource-bound assertion se pakda jaata hai.
why_needed: Index bugs aksar exception nahi dete; galat spot, kabhi kabhi LOT_FULL, ya dheere badhti memory. Har symptom ka cause jaanna debugging time bachata hai.
real_world_analogy: Khaali seats ki list: S8 bhari seat bata deti hai, S9 kuch khaali seats bhool jaati hai, S10 ek seat ka naam do baar likhti hai, S11 list ka order bigaad deti hai.
how_it_works: Oracle = brute-force scan (spots.find(free && size)) jo har step par index se compare hota hai. Resource bound = entryCount <= spots.
in_this_project: src/free-index.ts nearest(), released(), MinHeap.pop(); src/parking-lot.ts forget() mein this.index.released(spot) (S9 isi line ko hatata hai) aur reserve() ka STRATEGY_BUG check. test/free-index.test.ts scan aur entryCount assertions; test/invariants.test.ts expectedSpot.
advantages: Oracle test har bug ko 'galat answer' mein badal deta hai

question: In the stage 3 mutation run, S24 ('nearer' compares only the level) and S26 (spot.transfer does not check the holder) both survived with 0 failures. Why, and how were they closed?
answer_hinglish:
Dono test gaps the, code bugs nahi -- lekin agar asli bug hota toh tests chup rehte.

S24: nearer(a, b) level alag ho toh level compare karta hai, same level par position. Mutation ne sirf level compare kiya. Same level ke do spots par woh false deta, toh nearestFirst ka 'best' pehla mila size rehta. Allocation ka 'same level' test compact spot ko large se PEHLE rakhta tha -- sizes order mein (compact phir large) lene par sahi answer luck se aa gaya. Fix: test ab large spot ko NEARER rakhta hai (large at(0, 2), compact at(0, 5)) -- 'only a real position comparison picks it'. Ab S24 caught (1).

Interesting part: stage 2 par S24 ek test se pakda gaya tha aur README ki 'caught by exactly one test' list mein tha. Stage 3 par 0. README yeh nahi batata ki pehle kaunsa test pakadta tha, lekin lesson clear hai: ek-test wala catch ek rewrite se gayab ho sakta hai.

S26: spot.transfer(from, to) lost ticket par spot ko replacement ticket par le jaata hai, aur check karta hai ki spot occupied hai aur holder === from. Mutation ne holder check hataya. 0 failures kyunki kisi ne transfer ko galat ticket ke saath call hi nahi kiya -- reportLost hamesha sahi old.id deta hai. Fix: naya spot test 'transfer moves an occupied spot to a new ticket, only from its holder' -- transfer('x', 't2') SPOT_STATE throw kare aur heldBy 't1' hi rahe. Ab caught (1).

Debug approach: survivor dekho -> mutated line ko kaun sa test reach karta hai -> kya koi assertion us behaviour ko distinguish karta hai -> nahi toh aisa input banao jahan sahi aur galat code alag answer dein.
why_needed: Survivors batate hain ki ek guard ya rule bina test ke hai. Guard jaise transfer ka holder check tab tak 'dead code' lagta hai jab tak koi asli bug us par na gire.
real_world_analogy: S24: exam mein answer sahi aaya kyunki options ka order luckily sahi tha, samajh se nahi. S26: taala hai par kisi ne kabhi galat chaabi se khol ke check nahi kiya ki woh rokta hai.
how_it_works: Survivor ko kill karne ke liye aisa input chahiye jahan original aur mutant alag output dein. S24: same level, bada size nearer. S26: galat from-ticket.

question: In EventQueue.emit, why iterate over [...this.listeners] and then check this.listeners.has(listener) again?
answer_hinglish:
Do alag cheezein solve ho rahi hain, aur dono README ke rule hain: 'Unsubscribing during delivery takes effect at once; subscribing during delivery starts with the next event.'

Copy kyun: JavaScript ka Set iteration live hota hai -- agar loop chalte waqt Set mein naya element add ho, toh iterator use bhi visit karega. Matlab ek listener jo delivery ke beech kisi naye listener ko subscribe kare, woh naya listener CURRENT event bhi pa leta. Spread [...this.listeners] us moment ka snapshot banata hai, toh naya subscriber sirf agle event se shuru hota hai. Test: 'a listener subscribed during delivery gets the next event, not the current one' -- log [2] expect karta hai. Copy hatao toh [1, 2] aata; yeh mutation S14 tha (sirf 1 test ne pakda).

has() kyun: copy ki ek side effect hai -- agar listener A delivery ke beech listener B ko unsubscribe kare, toh B copy mein abhi bhi hai aur call ho jaata. has() check live Set dekhta hai aur B ko skip karta hai. Test: 'unsubscribing during delivery stops delivery to that listener at once' -- log [] expect. Yeh S15 tha.

Toh copy = 'naye log abhi nahi', has() = 'gaye hue log abhi se nahi'. Dono milke ek predictable rule dete hain. Cost: har event par listeners ki ek array copy -- listeners kam hain toh negligible.
why_needed: Listeners ke andar se subscribe/unsubscribe common hai (board close karna, ek-baar wala listener). Bina rule ke behaviour Set ke iteration details par depend karta.
real_world_analogy: Meeting mein attendance sheet ki photocopy se naam bulaate ho (beech mein aaye log agli meeting se), lekin har naam bulaane se pehle dekhte ho woh abhi bhi room mein hai ya chala gaya.
how_it_works: Snapshot array fixes who is eligible for this event; live has() removes anyone unsubscribed since the snapshot.
in_this_project: src/events.ts emit() comment: 'A copy, so subscribing during delivery does not add a listener to THIS event; the has() check skips a listener that was unsubscribed during delivery.' Tests test/events.test.ts. README mutations S14 (1 failure) aur S15.
advantages: Predictable subscribe/unsubscribe semantics
Simple: do lines
disadvantages: Har event par ek array allocation
Rule sirf tests se guarded -- S14 sirf ek test se
common_mistakes: Live Set par iterate karna
Copy rakh ke has() bhool jaana
Sochna ki Set iteration snapshot hota hai
follow_up_questions: Ek listener khud ko unsubscribe kare toh?
Same function do baar subscribe ho toh Set mein kya hoga?
unsubscribe idempotent kyun hai aur kaunsa test check karta hai?

question: Why is changeFree() the last line in reserve() and forget(), and why does it emit Object.freeze({ ...row }) instead of the row itself?
answer_hinglish:
Last isliye kyunki listener lot ko callback mein padh ya badal sakta hai, aur use ek consistent lot dikhna chahiye. Code comment: 'last: listeners see the finished change'. reserve() mein pehle ticket bana, spot.reserve(), entries aur ticketIdByPlate set, PHIR changeFree(spot, -1). forget() mein spot.release(), index.released(), entries aur plate index se hatana, PHIR changeFree(spot, +1).

Agar emit pehle ho jaaye (mutation S16 'reserve emits before the spot is taken', stage 2 par 11, stage 3 par 12 failures): listener ke time par spot abhi free dikhega aur plate abhi registered nahi. Valet jaisa listener jo lot.park() kare, usi spot ko chun sakta hai ya wahi plate dobara le sakta hai -- outer reserve ke liye state uske neeche se badal gaya. Lot ka 'check everything, then change' rule tab toot jaata hai.

Ek aur reason: lot ka promise hai ki thrown ParkingError = kuch nahi badla. Emit last hai aur EventQueue har listener error pakadta hai, toh emit ke baad kuch throw nahi ho sakta -- listener ki galti lot ke call ko fail nahi karti.

Freeze copy kyun: row lot ka internal mutable object hai (free += delta). Seedha dete toh listener row.free = 99 karke lot ke counts badal deta, ya board ek reference rakhta jo baad mein change ho jaata. Copy + freeze: listener ko us moment ki value milti hai aur likhne ki koshish TypeError (strict mode). Test: 'events are frozen copies: a listener cannot change the lot's counts'.
why_needed: Observer mein subject apna internal state leak kare ya adha-badla state dikhaye, toh bugs observers se wapas subject mein aate hain.
real_world_analogy: Bank statement ki photocopy (stamped, read-only) dete ho, passbook nahi; aur entry tab dete ho jab transaction poora ho chuka ho, beech mein nahi.
how_it_works: Mutate all internal state -> build an immutable snapshot of the affected row -> emit. Listener re-entering the lot sees a state where every check holds.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts reserve() 'this.changeFree(spot, -1); // last: listeners see the finished change', forget() 'this.changeFree(spot, +1); // last', changeFree() 'this.events.emit(Object.freeze({ ...row }))'. test/two-phase.test.ts 'events are frozen copies...' aur 'failed calls emit nothing'.
advantages: Listener hamesha consistent lot dekhta hai
Events immutable: lot ke counts safe
Failed call kabhi event nahi bhejta (emit sirf success path ke end mein)
disadvantages: Har event ek chhota object allocation
Freeze shallow hai -- nested objects hote toh deep freeze chahiye (yahan row flat hai)
common_mistakes: Emit ko method ke beech mein rakhna
Internal object seedha event mein dena
Sochna ki freeze non-strict code mein throw karega (wahan silently ignore hota hai)

confirm() emit kyun nahi karta?
Deep vs shallow freeze kab matter karta hai?

question: Read the randomized test in invariants.test.ts: what do rng(), the model, expectedSpot and checkInvariants each contribute?
answer_hinglish:
Yeh test 4 hisson se bana hai, aur har hissa ek alag cheez prove karta hai.

1. rng(seed) -- mulberry32, ek chhota seeded PRNG. Math.random nahi, kyunki failure reproducible chahiye: seed test ke naam mein hai ('seed 42: 500 steps...'), toh fail hua run exactly dobara chal sakta hai. Seeds 1, 2, 3, 42, 2026, dono strategies ke saath = 10 tests. (free-index.test.ts alag, ek simple LCG use karta hai seed 7 se.)

2. Model -- 'const model = new Map<string, Ticket>()': test ka apna simple record ki andar kaun hai. Har step ke baad lot.activeTickets.length === model.size. ALREADY_PARKED tabhi allowed jab model mein woh plate andar ho; plate space jaan bujh ke chhota (P0-P14) taaki yeh case hit ho.

3. expectedSpot -- ORACLE. Stage 1 ka algorithm (har free spot scan) yahan test mein zinda rakha gaya: 'The stage 1 algorithm (scan every spot), kept here as the oracle for the index.' Har park ka spotId is se match hona chahiye, aur LOT_FULL tabhi jab oracle bhi undefined de.

4. checkInvariants -- rules jo har step ke baad sach hone chahiye: free spot ka holder null; reserved spot ka ticket 'reserved' status mein; har active ticket ka spot occupied, usi ka, aur fit karta hai; koi plate do baar nahi; board ke free ka sum == free spots; aur board.rows() == availability() ('the Observer never drifted').

Aakhri line 'expect(full).toBeGreaterThan(0)' -- test khud prove karta hai ki run full lot tak pahuncha, warna LOT_FULL path kabhi test hi nahi hota.
why_needed: Example tests sirf woh cases check karte hain jo author ne soche. Random steps + invariants + oracle un sequences ko bhi check karte hain jo kisi ne socha nahi -- jaise S9 jo sirf specific pop/release order mein dikhta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek auditor jo roz random transactions chalata hai, har ke baad ledger ko apne simple hisaab (model) aur purane manual tareeke (oracle) se milaata hai, aur kuch golden rules (invariants) check karta hai.
how_it_works: Loop: advance clock randomly -> 45% exit a random parked car, else park a random vehicle/plate -> compare with oracle/model -> checkInvariants. Concurrent variant: 3 entry + 2 exit gates, pending device calls settled in random order, 15% failures; har pending call ke peeche claim hona chahiye.
in_this_project: test/invariants.test.ts: function rng(seed) (mulberry32), LAYOUT (2 levels), expectedSpot(), checkInvariants(), describe.each smallestFitFirst/nearestFirst with seeds [1, 2, 3, 42, 2026] x 500 steps; 'random concurrent gates' seeds [5..9] x 400 steps. README: 15 tests in this file.

Oracle index ki har galti ko galat spotId mein badal deta hai
Board drift har step par pakda jaata hai
disadvantages: Oracle aur LAYOUT fixed hain -- jaise LAYOUT mein har level par compact large se pehle hai, toh S24 jaisi galti yahan nahi dikhti
Failure par shrinking (minimal case) nahi, jaise property-testing libraries dete hain

Sirf final state check karna, har step nahi
Yeh check na karna ki random run interesting states (full lot) tak pahuncha
follow_up_questions: fast-check jaisi property-testing library kya extra deti?
Oracle bhi galat ho toh?
Concurrent test 'every outstanding device call is backed by a claim' kaise check karta hai?

question: Write a LevelBoard observer that shows free/total per level (all sizes together), and a test that it follows park and exit.
answer_hinglish:
Approach: DisplayBoard wala hi pattern -- availability() se start, phir sirf events. Lekin events ek (level, size) row ka ABSOLUTE count dete hain, delta nahi. Toh main level ka running total +1/-1 nahi karunga; main per-row latest value rakhunga aur level totals read ke time par jodunga. Isse duplicate ya re-ordered event ka asar bhi limited rehta hai, aur code DisplayBoard jaisa simple.

Kyun delta wala galat hoga: event mein 'free: 3' aata hai, 'free changed by -1' nahi. Delta nikaalne ke liye purani value chahiye -- jo phir bhi per-row rakhni padegi. Toh per-row map hi asli state hai.

levels() rows ko level ke hisaab se group karta hai. Rows lot ke order mein insert hui hain (level 0 pehle), aur Map existing key par set() se order nahi badalta, toh levels ka order bhi stable.

Test: do levels, truck park karo -- woh level 1 ke large mein jaayega (sirf wahi fit), level 1 ka free 1 hona chahiye. Exit ke baad wapas 2. ManualClock use kiya taaki fee deterministic rahe (0 ms stay, grace 0 -> fee 0, exit() kuch collect nahi karta). Aur close() ke baad board update nahi hona chahiye.

Extra check jo main add karunga: ek randomized run mein levels() ko availability() se aggregate karke compare -- invariants test ki tarah.
why_needed: Real lots mein entrance par per-floor board hota hai ('Level 2: 14 free'). Exercise Observer contract (absolute rows) ko samajhne ka test hai.
real_world_analogy: Har floor ke counters ka total main gate par: floor managers apne size-wise numbers bhejte hain, main gate board unko jod ke dikhata hai.
how_it_works: State: Map<'level:size', Availability>. Event: set. Read: group by level, sum free and total.

Absolute rows se state simple
Read O(rows), update O(1)

Size-wise detail kho jaati hai

Test mein systemClock use karna -- fee aur cash payment non-deterministic

question: The README says the free-spot index is not benchmarked. Write a benchmark harness that compares FreeSpotIndex.nearest() with the stage 1 full scan, fairly.
answer_hinglish:
Pehle disclaimer: is harness ka koi result repo mein nahi hai, aur main koi number claim nahi kar raha -- yeh sirf code hai jo measure KAREGA.

Fair benchmark ke rules jo main follow karunga:
1. Same workload dono ke liye: same seeded PRNG (mulberry32, invariants test wala), same spots, same sequence of take/release. Checksum (chune gaye spots ki positions ka sum) dono modes mein equal hona chahiye -- isse pata chalta hai dono ne same kaam kiya, aur benchmark ek correctness check bhi ban jaata hai.
2. Realistic occupancy: scan ka cost isse depend karta hai ki pehla free spot kitna door hai. Nearest-first allocation aage ke spots bhar deta hai, toh scan bhari prefix par chalta hai. Random fill se scan unfairly fast dikh sakta hai. Isliye warm-up phase mein allocation khud lot bharti hai, aur phir measured phase mein take/release mix.
3. Warm-up run (JIT), phir kai seeds, median report.
4. N vary karo (100 se 100,000) -- complexity ka claim tabhi dikhta hai jab N badhe.
5. Index mode mein released() ka cost bhi gina jaaye, kyunki asli lot mein woh bhi lagta hai.

File src/ mein rakhi toh 'npm run build' use dist mein compile karega aur 'node dist/bench-free-index.js' se chalegi. Behtar: alag bench/ folder aur apna tsconfig, taaki library build mein bench na jaaye.

real_world_analogy: Do routes ka time naapna ho toh dono ko same din, same traffic, same gaadi se chalao, kai baar, aur median lo -- ek baar khaali sadak par ek ko aur rush hour mein doosre ko nahi.

question: For delivering availability events you could use nested synchronous calls, a synchronous queue, or asynchronous delivery. Why the queue here?
answer_hinglish:
Teen options aur unka trade-off:

1. Nested synchronous (plain Observer, jaise Node ka EventEmitter -- emit listeners ko turant call karta hai): simplest. Problem re-entrancy: listener A event 1 handle karte hue lot badle, toh event 2 baaki listeners ko event 1 se PEHLE mil jaata hai. Board B pehle 2 dekhta, phir purana 1, aur stale count par atak jaata. Mutation S12 ne yahi kiya, 2 tests fail.

2. Synchronous queue (chosen): emit enqueue karta hai; jo emit pehle se deliver nahi kar raha woh drain karta hai. Har event poore listeners tak pahunchta hai, phir agla. Global order = changes ka order. Delivery ab bhi synchronous hai, toh lot method return hone tak sab listeners updated hain -- tests seedha 'park ke baad board == availability()' check kar sakte hain.

3. Async (queueMicrotask / setImmediate): lot ka call fast, slow listener lot ko nahi rokta. Lekin: listener jab chalega tab lot event se aage nikal chuka ho sakta hai; tests ko await karna padega; ordering ab scheduler par; aur listener ki error lot ke call stack se bahar.

Is project mein listeners sasta kaam karte hain (DisplayBoard ka Map.set) aur sab ek process mein hai, toh async ka fayda kam, cost zyada. Queue ne re-entrancy ka asli bug theek kiya bina timing badle. PLAN: 'Without the queue, a listener that changes the lot inside its handler makes later listeners receive the newer event first and end on a stale count (tested).'
why_needed: Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki tum Observer ka re-entrancy problem jaante ho aur bina zaroorat async complexity nahi laate.
real_world_analogy: Nested: speaker ke beech koi doosra mic chheen ke bolne lage. Queue: 'aapki baari iske baad'. Async: speech record karke baad mein bhejna -- sab sunenge, par jab sunenge tab tak situation badal chuki ho sakti hai.
how_it_works: Queue + delivering flag converts re-entrant emits into FIFO deliveries within the same synchronous call. Async would move delivery to a later tick.
in_this_project: src/events.ts top comment 'Why a queue'; PLAN 'Stage 2: Observer with a queue'; test/events.test.ts queue order test aur re-entrant valet test; README 'Events are queued: if a listener changes the lot inside its handler, the new event is delivered after the current one reached every listener'.
advantages: Order guaranteed aur re-entrancy safe
Synchronous: method return = sab listeners updated
Koi scheduler/timer nahi
disadvantages: Slow listener ab bhi lot ko rokta hai
Re-entrant listener ka nested park() turant return karta hai par uska event baad mein deliver hota hai -- listener ko yeh samajhna padta hai
common_mistakes: Queue ko async samajhna
Async delivery ko 'free performance' samajhna bina ordering/consistency socha
Re-entrant case ko test na karna

Node EventEmitter ke saath yeh bug kaise reproduce karoge?
Listener lot mein har event par change kare toh loop kab rukega?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Queue: correctness (order) bina timing change ke. Async: decoupling aur latency, lekin consistency aur testability ki keemat par. Process ke andar sasta listener = queue sahi.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Queue ke saath bhi ek listener jo har event par lot badle (aur har badlaav event de) delivery loop ko lamba ya infinite kar sakta hai. Nested ke saath stale boards. Async ke saath listener lot ki 'future' state padhta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Async queue with sequence numbers (listeners order verify karein); events ko batch karke ek tick par deliver karna; ya external broker agar listeners doosre processes mein hain.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Listeners aur events zyada hon toh synchronous delivery lot ki latency badhaayegi; tab ek single fan-out listener jo async sender ko feed kare.
advanced.production_improvements: Re-entrancy depth ka guard/metric, per-listener time, aur network boards ke liye sequence-numbered async channel.

question: In stage 2 the allocation strategy stopped receiving a list of free spots and now only gets FreeSpots.nearest(size). What did that interface change buy, and what did it cost?
answer_hinglish:
Fayda: performance aur simplicity. PLAN kehta hai: 'park() goes from O(spots) to O(sizes x log spots). The interface change was worth it: a strategy now says only WHICH SIZE it prefers'. smallestFitFirst ab sirf fittingSizes(vehicle) loop karke pehla mila spot return karta hai; nearestFirst har fitting size ka nearest leke nearer() se compare karta hai. Dono 10 lines se kam.

Doosra fayda testability: FreeSpots ek one-method interface hai, toh allocation.test.ts real index ke bina ek hand-made free(map) se strategies test karta hai -- exact inputs, jaise S24 ko close karne wala 'nearer large beats further compact' case. Aur lot strategy par bharosa nahi karta: jo bhi spot aaye, check karta hai ki woh isi lot ka, free aur fitting hai, warna STRATEGY_BUG.

Cost: strategy ki expressive power kam ho gayi. Ab strategy sirf yeh pooch sakti hai 'size X ka nearest free'. Agar kal rule aaye 'levels par load spread karo', 'lift ke paas wala', 'EV spot pehle', ya 'nearest to THIS entrance' -- inmein se koi bhi sirf nearest(size) se nahi banta. Interface badhana padega (jaise nearest(size, level) ya per-entrance index), aur har naye method ke saath index ko bhi efficient rakhna hoga.

Mera view: LLD mein interface ko current requirements ke liye narrow rakhna sahi hai, jab tak extension ka raasta clear hai. Yahan woh clear hai: FreeSpots badhao, aur oracle test ko naye rule ke scan se compare karo. Multi-entrance aur doosre rules is repo mein implement nahi hain.
why_needed: Interface ka shape decide karta hai ki kaunsi policies sasti hain aur kaunsi possible hi nahi. Senior engineer ko dono side batani chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Pehle valet ko poori parking ki list milti thi -- jo chahe chune, par har baar poori list padhe. Ab valet sirf counter se poochta hai 'compact ka sabse paas wala?' -- tez hai, par 'kahin bhi jahan chhaon ho' nahi pooch sakta.
how_it_works: Policy (which size, in which order) strategy mein; mechanism (nearest free of a size, fast) index mein. Lot validates the result.
in_this_project: src/free-index.ts 'export interface FreeSpots { nearest(size: SpotSize): ParkingSpot | undefined; }'. src/allocation.ts AllocationStrategy.choose(vehicle, free: FreeSpots), smallestFitFirst, nearestFirst. src/parking-lot.ts reserve() STRATEGY_BUG check. test/allocation.test.ts free(map) helper. PLAN Decisions 'Stage 2: strategies ask an index, not a list.'
advantages: O(sizes x log spots) per park
Strategies tiny aur bina index ke testable
Policy aur mechanism alag
disadvantages: Sirf 'nearest of size' expressible
Naya rule = interface + index dono badlenge
nearestFirst ka 'nearer' hard-coded level/position par
common_mistakes: Interface ko pehle se har future rule ke liye bada bana dena (YAGNI)
Strategy ko index ka internal (heaps) de dena
Strategy result validate na karna
follow_up_questions: 'Spread load across levels' strategy ke liye FreeSpots mein kya add karoge?
Strategy ko poora lot de dete toh kya problem hoti?
STRATEGY_BUG check strategy ke andar kyun nahi, lot mein kyun?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Narrow interface = fast aur safe, lekin naye rules ke liye extension. Wide interface (list ya poora lot) = flexible, lekin har strategy O(spots) aur lot ke internals se coupled.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Ek third-party strategy galat spot de (taken, non-fitting, doosre lot ka) -- lot STRATEGY_BUG deta hai aur kuch nahi badalta (tested, S22 'spot of another lot accepted' 1 test se caught). Strategy undefined de jabki spot free hai -- bhi STRATEGY_BUG, kyunki lot pehle LOT_FULL khud check karta hai.
advanced.alternatives: FreeSpots mein nearest(size, level) ya iterate(size) (lazy iterator, nearest first) add karna; ya strategy ko read-only snapshot dena aur sirf chhote lots par allow karna.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bade lot par list-based interface wapas O(spots) par le jaata; narrow interface hi scale karta hai. Kai entrances ke liye FreeSpots per entrance.
advanced.production_improvements: Strategy ke liye ek contract test suite (koi bhi naya strategy unhi tests se guzre), aur oracle test ko har strategy ke brute-force version ke saath parametrize karna.

question: Real display boards are separate devices on a network. How would you extend 'start from availability(), then apply events' so boards stay correct across a network?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle: yeh built nahi hai. Aaj DisplayBoard usi process mein hai, aur uska snapshot + subscribe ek synchronous constructor mein hota hai -- beech mein koi event miss nahi ho sakta. Network par yeh guarantee chali jaati hai, aur teen problems aati hain: snapshot aur subscribe ke beech gap, lost events, aur reordered events. DisplayBoard ka comment khud kehta hai: 'If an event were lost or delivered out of order, the board would drift'.

Mera design:
1. Lot har event par ek monotonic sequence number lagaye (lot-wide counter). Event mein already absolute row hai (free, total), delta nahi -- yeh bahut kaam aata hai, kyunki duplicate event dobara apply karna harmless hai.
2. Snapshot bhi usi sequence ke saath: availability() + 'yeh state seq N tak ki hai'.
3. Board connect hote hi pehle subscribe kare (events buffer kare), phir snapshot le, phir buffer se sirf seq > N wale apply kare. Isse gap band.
4. Board har event ka seq check kare: seq == last + 1 toh apply; gap dikhe toh resync (naya snapshot). Purana seq aaye toh ignore.
5. Board offline ho ke wapas aaye toh simply resync -- absolute rows ki wajah se replay ki zaroorat nahi.

Transport: lot process ke andar ek listener events ko outbox/broker mein daale (cheap, synchronous), aur network sender alag. Kaafi boards ke liye pub/sub. Yeh sab standard snapshot-plus-log pattern hai; is repo mein sirf in-process version hai aur randomized test board ko availability() se har step par compare karta hai.
why_needed: Senior round mein in-process Observer ko distributed banana common follow-up hai, aur snapshot+delta sync har jagah aata hai (caches, replicas, UIs).
real_world_analogy: Live cricket score app: app khulte hi current scorecard leta hai (snapshot, over 14.3 tak), phir ball-by-ball updates; agar 14.5 ke baad seedha 15.2 aaye toh app samajh jaata hai beech mein kuch miss hua aur scorecard dobara mangta hai.
how_it_works: Versioned snapshot + sequenced event stream; subscribe-before-snapshot with buffering; gap detection -> resync; absolute values make duplicates idempotent.
in_this_project: src/display-board.ts constructor (availability() phir lot.subscribe) aur drift wala comment; src/parking-lot.ts AvailabilityChanged = Availability (absolute row); test/invariants.test.ts checkInvariants 'the Observer never drifted'. Sequence numbers, network transport, resync -- kuch bhi implement nahi hai.
advantages: Gap aur reorder detect hote hain
Absolute rows se duplicates idempotent
Board restart = sirf resync
disadvantages: Lot ko seq counter aur versioned snapshot dena padega (API change)
Resync storms agar network flaky ho
Ek aur moving part: broker/outbox
common_mistakes: Snapshot pehle, subscribe baad mein -- beech ke events gayab
Delta events bhejna (+1/-1) -- ek lost event permanent galti
Sequence numbers ke bina 'TCP order deta hai' maan lena (reconnect par nahi)
follow_up_questions: Kai lot processes hon toh sequence number kaun dega?
Boards ke liye push vs poll (har 5 sec availability()) -- kab kya?
Board ki staleness ko user ko kaise dikhaoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Push + seq + resync: fresh aur efficient, lekin complex. Simple polling of availability() (O(rows)) kuch seconds par: boards ke liye aksar kaafi aur bahut simple -- parking board ko millisecond freshness nahi chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Broker down: boards stale, reconnect par resync. Lot process restart: seq counter reset -- board ko epoch/lot-instance id bhi chahiye warna naya seq 0 'old' lagega. Snapshot aur events alag sources se aayein toh inconsistent.
advanced.alternatives: Periodic polling; server-sent events / websockets with seq; ya CRDT-like absolute state broadcast (har kuch seconds poori availability, chhoti hai).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Rows kam hain (levels x sizes), toh poori availability broadcast karna bhi sasta hai -- bahut boards par periodic full-state broadcast seq logic se simpler ho sakta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Lot-instance epoch + seq, board par 'last updated' indicator, staleness alarm, aur ek reconciliation test jo random disconnects ke saath board ko availability() se compare kare.

question: Who owns what between ParkingLot, FreeSpotIndex, EventQueue and DisplayBoard? Draw the relationships.
answer_hinglish:
ParkingLot centre mein hai aur baaki teen ke saath alag relationship hai.

ParkingLot OWNS FreeSpotIndex: constructor mein spots banane ke baad 'this.index = new FreeSpotIndex(this.spots)'. Lot index ko do kaam ke liye use karta hai -- LOT_FULL pre-check aur strategy ko pass karna (choose(vehicle, this.index)) -- aur har free hone par index.released(spot) batata hai. Strategy ko index sirf FreeSpots interface ke through dikhta hai (sirf nearest()).

ParkingLot OWNS EventQueue: 'this.events = new EventQueue(onError)', jahan onError options.onListenerError hai ya default console.error. Lot bahar sirf subscribe() deta hai; emit() private path changeFree() se hi hota hai. Bahar wala event bhej nahi sakta.

DisplayBoard USES ParkingLot: woh lot ke bahar hai, lot ko uska pata nahi. Board availability() aur subscribe() -- do public methods -- use karta hai. Isi wajah se board badle toh lot nahi badalta.

Source of truth: spot ka free/reserved/occupied ParkingSpot mein; index sirf ordering ka cache; rows Map (counts) lot mein; board ki copy events se. README ka class diagram yahi dikhata hai: 'ParkingLot ... owns 1 FreeSpotIndex' aur 'DisplayBoard (Observer) ^ subscribe(): availability events'.

Rule: dependencies ek taraf -- board -> lot -> index/queue. Index aur queue lot ko nahi jaante; EventQueue generic EventQueue<E> hai, lot-specific kuch nahi.
why_needed: LLD round ka pehla sawaal: classes aur unki responsibilities. Ownership clear ho toh change ka asar bhi clear hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Lot ek building manager: uske paas khaali spots ki register (index) aur announcement system (queue) hai. Lobby ka display board ek bahar ka vendor hai jo sirf announcements sunta hai.
how_it_works: Composition: lot creates and holds index and queue privately. Observer: board subscribes via the lot's public API. Interfaces: strategy sees FreeSpots, board sees Availability events.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts constructor: 'this.index = new FreeSpotIndex(this.spots)' aur 'this.events = new EventQueue(onError)'; subscribe(); availability(). src/display-board.ts DisplayBoard(lot). README 'Classes' diagram aur Files table.
advantages: One-way dependencies
Index aur queue reusable/generic
Board lot ke internals se independent
disadvantages: Lot ko index.released() aur changeFree() dono yaad rakhne padte hain har free/take par
Index aur counters dono derived state -- dono ko test se guard karna padta hai
common_mistakes: Board ko lot ke andar bana dena (lot ko board ka pata)
Index ko public bana dena taaki koi bhi push kare
Kisi ko bhi emit() karne dena
follow_up_questions: Index ko lot ke bahar inject karna ho (testing ke liye) toh?
onListenerError default console.error kyun, throw kyun nahi?
Level class kyun nahi banayi? (PLAN dekho)
